title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 — Mock Test 1

questions.stem: In a code, 'PEACE' = 'QFBDF'. How is 'WORLD' coded?

questions.stem: Pointing to a man, Asha said, 'He is the only son of my mother's mother's son.' How is the man related to Asha?
questions.explanation: Asha's mother's mother = Asha's maternal grandmother. The only son of grandmother = Asha's maternal uncle. The only son of Asha's maternal uncle = Asha's cousin (specifically male cousin).
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A is the brother of B, B is the wife of C, and C is the father of D, how is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is D's father. B is C's wife → B is D's mother. A is B's brother → A is D's maternal uncle.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A man walks 6 km west, then 8 km north. What is his shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All birds are animals. All animals breathe air.
Conclusions:
I. All birds breathe air.
II. Some animals are birds.
questions.explanation: Birds ⊂ animals; animals breathe air ⟹ all birds breathe air (I). Birds exist as a subset of animals ⟹ some animals are birds (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some books are pens. No pen is a pencil.
Conclusions:
I. Some books are not pencils.
II. No book is a pencil.
questions.explanation: Some books are pens; no pen is a pencil ⟹ those books (the ones that are pens) are not pencils ⟹ I follows. But other books (not pens) might still be pencils, so II is too strong. DOES NOT FOLLOW.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All apples are fruits. Some fruits are sweet.
Conclusions:
I. Some apples are sweet.
II. All apples are sweet.
questions.explanation: We only know SOME fruits are sweet — those sweet fruits might or might not include any apples. Neither 'some apples sweet' nor 'all apples sweet' is guaranteed. Neither follows.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All flowers are plants. No plant is an animal.
Conclusions:
I. No flower is an animal.
II. Some plants are flowers.
questions.explanation: Flowers ⊂ plants; plants disjoint from animals ⟹ flowers disjoint from animals (I follows). Flowers exist as plants ⟹ some plants are flowers (II follows). Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All metals are conductors. Some conductors are heavy.
Conclusions:
I. Some metals are heavy.
II. All conductors are metals.
questions.explanation:
I. Heavy conductors might or might not include metals. NOT guaranteed.
II. Metals are conductors but converse-fallacy: SOME conductors might not be metals. NOT guaranteed.
Neither follows.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: P ≥ Q > R ≤ S; T < R; U > S
Conclusions:
I. P > T
II. U > R
questions.explanation:
I. P ≥ Q > R > T ⟹ P > T. FOLLOWS.
II. U > S ≥ R ⟹ U > R. FOLLOWS. Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people — A, B, C, D, E — sit in a row facing North. C sits at one end. A is to the immediate right of E. B is between A and D. Where does D sit?
questions.explanation: C at one end. Try C@1: positions 2-5 for others. A immediately right of E ⟹ E and A consecutive (E left of A). B between A and D. Trying E@2, A@3, B@4, D@5. Check: B between A(3) and D(5)? Position 4 is between, ✓. C@1, E@2, A@3, B@4, D@5. D at right end. ✓
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six people sit around a circular table facing the centre. P opposite Q. R immediate right of P. S between Q and R. T sits next to Q. U occupies the remaining seat. Who sits opposite R?
questions.explanation: P @ 1, Q opposite @ 4. R immediate right of P (clockwise) → R @ 6. S between Q and R: clockwise from R(6) → 5 → 4(Q), so S @ 5. T next to Q: T @ 3 (since 5 taken). U @ 2. Final: 1=P, 2=U, 3=T, 4=Q, 5=S, 6=R. Opposite R(6) = seat 3 = T.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people — A, B, C, D, E — live on 5 floors (1=ground, 5=top). A lives above C. D lives below B. E lives on the topmost floor. Which two consecutive floors do A and B live on?
questions.explanation: E=5. Remaining floors 1-4 for A, B, C, D. A>C, B>D. Several arrangements satisfy all constraints (e.g. C=1,A=4,D=2,B=3 or C=1,A=2,D=3,B=4 etc.). Position of A and B is not unique. Cannot be determined.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Four friends — P, Q, R, S — were born in different months: January, April, July, October. P was born before Q. R was born immediately after P. S was born after R. Who was born in October?
questions.explanation:
P < R (R immediately after P), R < S. So P < R < S in month order. P < Q gives Q > P only.
The unique increasing assignment of P, R, S over three of the four months — placing Q in the remaining slot:
P=Jan, R=Apr, S=Jul, Q=Oct. (Q=Oct satisfies Q > P.) So Q was born in October.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
What is the average age of A, B, and C?
I. Sum of ages = 90 years.
II. The youngest is 20 years old.
options: Both I and II together are needed
Neither I nor II is sufficient
questions.explanation: From I: average = 90/3 = 30. ✓ Sufficient. From II alone: only one age, insufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
How many sisters does Ankit have?
I. Ankit's father has 4 children.
II. Ankit's father has 2 sons.
options: Both I and II together are needed
Neither I nor II is sufficient
questions.explanation: I alone: 4 children but unknown gender split. II alone: 2 sons but unknown total. Together: 4 − 2 = 2 sisters (Ankit is one of the 2 sons). Sufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the change in India's payment landscape?
questions.passage_context: The growth of digital payments in India has been nothing short of transformative. From a cash-dominated economy a decade ago, India now leads the world in real-time transaction volumes, with UPI alone processing tens of billions of transactions every month. The rapid adoption has democratised financial services, bringing credit and small-ticket commerce within reach of millions who were previously outside the formal system. However, this scale comes with risks: cyber-fraud has risen in tandem with adoption, and many users — especially those new to digital banking — fall prey to social-engineering scams. questions.stem:
Rearrange to form a meaningful paragraph and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) However, the recent push for vocational training is encouraging.
(B) For decades, India's school curriculum focused almost exclusively on rote learning.
(C) Skill development was rarely treated as part of mainstream education.
(D) Reforms now aim to bridge the gap between classroom learning and employability.
(E) New National Education Policy targets a fundamental shift in this regard.
questions.explanation: Logical order: B (general claim about decades-old focus) → C (consequence: skill rarely mainstream) → A (However = contrast: recent encouraging push) → E (concrete policy reference) → D (specific aim of reforms). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange to form a meaningful paragraph and identify the LAST sentence.

(A) The plan was promptly approved by the committee.
(B) The next step is implementation across all departments.
(C) The proposal received unanimous support from members.
(D) A senior official presented the strategic plan.
(E) Detailed timelines have already been shared with each team.
questions.explanation: Logical order: D (presentation) → C (unanimous support) → A (plan approved) → E (timelines shared) → B (next step is implementation). Last = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH
